newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong's Tung inspects Chinese PLA troops.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Tung inspects Chinese PLA troops.

text.p: China's People's Liberation Army rolled out the red carpet for Hong Kong leader Tung Chee-hwa when he inspected the troops on Wednesday on his first visit to the new PLA garrison in the former British colony.

Garrison commander Major-General Liu Zhenwu took the opportunity to reassure Hong Kong people that his troops would strictly abide by the capitalist territory's laws and respect its freewheeling ways.

Under the terms of Hong Kong's reversion to Chinese rule last week, Beijing is to allow it broad autonomy for 50 years in running its own affairs, with the central government responsible only for defence and foreign affairs.
A brass band welcomed Tung and top government officials to the new Chinese navy base on Stonecutters Island, in Hong Kong's Victoria harbour.

Garrison chief Liu and his top brass gave a warm welcome to Tung and his entourage, including popular Chief Secretary Anson Chan, Financial Secretary Donald Tsang, Security Secretary Peter Lai and Police Commissioner Eddie Hui.
After passing through an honour guard of army, air and naval troops, the visitors boarded a missile frigate, one of four plying Hong Kong waters since the territory reverted to China on July 1.
Officers gave Tung's group a tour of the ship, which carries six missile launchers. Tung also inspected a support ship.

In a speech, General Liu pointedly gave guarantees to Hong Kong people on the benign role his 5,000-strong force would play in the territory, where many recall with trepidation how the PLA opened fire on unarmed student protesters around Beijing's Tiananmen Square in June 1989.
"We will not interfere in the internal affairs of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR)," he said.
"We will not create troubles for the Hong Kong SAR government. We will respect Hong Kong's way of life and the rule of law," Liu added.
Tung said the territory's 6.4 million people would grow to trust the Chinese armed forces.
"From now on Hong Kong people and the PLA Garrison drink from the same well," the new chief executive told the troops.
"Although we have different tasks, different cultural backgrounds and different experiences, we have the same responsibility to ensure Hong Kong's stability and prosperity."
